I would keep it simple and stay with the pattern I know best in Quzhou: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is the steadiest way for me to use the full year, match our local climate on the North China Plain, and avoid taking extra market risk. I would not spread myself too thin with too many crops. I know how to manage wheat and maize, I can line up seed, fertilizer, irrigation, and labor for them, and I trust that rotation more than experimenting. For wheat, I would focus on strong seed, one solid basal fertilizer application plus topdressing nitrogen at jointing, watch aphids and rust, and irrigate at the key stages. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize with hybrid seed, enough nitrogen for vegetative growth and ear filling, fewer irrigation rounds than wheat unless the summer turns dry, and pest control mainly for borers and leaf pests. I would use rotary tillage because it is faster, cheaper for me, and fits the pace between the wheat harvest and maize sowing.
